Reading a Migration →

prisma migrate dev

One command: diff the schema, generate SQL, apply it, and keep a record of what changed.

An Artisan migration is something you write — PHP describing a schema change, run with php artisan migrate. Prisma migrations work the other way around: you edit schema.prisma to describe the shape you want, and prisma migrate dev figures out — and writes — the SQL needed to get the real database there, by comparing the schema against what's already been applied.

npx prisma migrate dev --name init

--name init just labels this migration for the (human-readable) folder name it creates — the next slide looks at what that folder actually contains. Running it against this project's finished schema produces something close to:

Applying migration `20260909122353_init`

The following migration(s) have been created and applied from new schema
changes:

prisma/migrations/
  └─ 20260909122353_init/
    └─ migration.sql

Your database is now in sync with your schema.

Two things happened in one command: a new .sql file was generated and immediately run against the MySQL container from the Docker topic. migrate dev is explicitly the development command — safe to run repeatedly as your schema changes while you're building. (A separate migrate deploy exists for production, which only ever applies migrations already generated this way — never generates new ones on the fly there.)
